[id="oci-storage-configuration-parameters_{context}"]
= OCI storage configuration and connection parameters

[role="_abstract"]
You can configure OCI-compliant storage for Model Registry by using the following parameters.
The parameters are organized by scope: administrator configuration parameters for the storage backend and user-facing parameters for the OCI image format and authentication.

[id="admin-configuration-parameters_{context}"]
== Administrator configuration parameters

Administrators use the following parameters to enable and configure OCI storage for Model Registry.

// TODO: SME verification required (RHOAIENG-16840 tech review C1).
// The `registryOciStorage` parameter does not exist in the odh-dashboard
// source code. If confirmed non-existent downstream, remove the first row.
.Administrator configuration parameters for OCI storage
[cols="1,1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Parameter
|Type
|Default
|Description

|`registryOciStorage`
|Boolean
|`false`
|Enables the OCI storage feature in the {productname-short} dashboard. Set this parameter to `true` in the `spec.dashboardConfig` section of the `OdhDashboardConfig` custom resource.

|Registry endpoint URL
|String
|None
|The URL of the OCI-compliant registry, for example `quay.io` or your self-hosted registry hostname.

|Authentication credential format
|Secret
|None
|A Kubernetes Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` that contains base64-encoded authentication data for the target OCI registry.

|Connection type
|String
|None
|The type of OCI connection. Use `OCI compliant registry v1` for private registries that require authentication, or `URI v1` for public registries that do not require authentication.
|===

[id="model-transfer-job-parameters_{context}"]
== Model transfer job parameters

The model transfer job is a background Kubernetes Job that copies model files from a source location, packages them as a `ModelCar` OCI image, and pushes the image to the OCI registry.

.Model transfer job parameters
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Parameter
|Type
|Description

|Job display name
|String
|A human-readable name for the transfer job, for example `Upload granite-7b to Quay`.

|Job resource name
|String
|A valid Kubernetes resource name for the Job, autogenerated from the display name. You can edit this value.

|Namespace
|String
|The Kubernetes namespace where the transfer job runs. The namespace must have access to the model registry instance.
|===

[id="oci-uri-format-parameters_{context}"]
== OCI URI format

After a model is stored as an OCI image, the artifact URI in Model Registry uses the following format:

----
oci://<registry>/<organization>/<repository>:<tag>
----

For example: `oci://quay.io/myorg/granite-7b:v1`.

For Quay destinations, {productname-short} automatically uses `quay.io/quay/busybox:latest` as the base image for `ModelCar` construction.
For other registries, the base image depends on the default configured in the model-sync container.

[id="supported-oci-registries-reference_{context}"]
== Supported registries

.Supported OCI registries for model storage
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Registry
|Version requirement
|Notes

|Red Hat Quay
|3.11 or later
|OCI artifact support is enabled by default. Supports robot accounts for service authentication.

|Customer-provided OCI-compliant registries
|Must support the OCI Distribution Specification
|Requires a container image such as `busybox:latest` to be accessible as the `ModelCar` base image.
|===

[id="oci-authentication-methods_{context}"]
== Authentication methods

You can authenticate to the OCI registry by using one of the following methods:

.OCI registry authentication methods
[cols="1,2,1", options="header"]
|===
|Method
|Description
|Use case

|Kubernetes Secret (`.dockerconfigjson`)
|A Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` stores base64-encoded registry credentials. The dashboard creates this Secret automatically when you configure an *OCI compliant registry v1* connection.
|Dashboard UI transfer jobs

|Pre-existing login
|Authenticate to the registry by using `skopeo login` or `podman login` before running the Python client. The existing credentials are used automatically.
|Python client (workbench environments)

|Environment variable
|Set an environment variable that points to a file containing credentials in `.dockerconfigjson` format. Pass the variable name to `oci_auth_env_var` in `OCIParams`.
|Python client (automated pipelines)

|Username and password
|Pass the registry username and password directly to the `oci_username` and `oci_password` parameters in `OCIParams`.
|Python client (interactive use)
|===

[id="backend-cli-tools_{context}"]
== Backend CLI tools for the Python client

The Python client uses an external CLI tool to push OCI images to the registry.

.Supported backend CLI tools
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Tool
|OCIParams value
|Notes

|`skopeo`
|`skopeo` (default)
|The default backend. Must be installed and available in your `PATH`.

|`oras`
|`oras`
|An alternative backend. Must be installed and available in your `PATH`.
|===
